To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. Dietary weight management is targeted at the reduction of energy intake, especially fat intake, 2. The intake of simple carbohydrates should be reduced in the treatment of obesity, 3. Dietary protein positively affect the outcome of weight loss,

the intake of fat, saturated fatty acids, simple carbohydrate, low glycaemic index carbohydrate and high glycaemic carbohydrates, as well as the low intake of protein, calcium, phosphate, n-3 fatty acid, fibre, n-3 PUFA and vitamin A are associated with obesity and metabolic syndrome and that the intake of n-3 fatty acis and protein are associated with the positive outcome of weight management.

the intake of fat, especially saturated fat, simple carbohydrates, low-fibre carbohydrates and alcohol should be restricted in the weight management and the consumption of protein, n-3 fatty acid, calcium, phosphate and vitamins should be increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of individual dietary nutrients on the weight management and the metabolic consequences of the obesity.
the role of nutritional factors (fat, carbohydrate, protein and vitamins) in the weight management.
the role of nutritional factors in weight management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dietary strategies for weight management should be based on the reduction of the intake of energy-dense foods and on the reduction of simple carbohydrates and saturated fat intake.
dietary weight management should be based on the reduction of energy intake, reduction of fat intake and the intake of specific macronutrients and micronutrients with specific metabolic effects.

dietary weight management should be targeted on the reduction of energy density of diet through the reduction of fat and simple carbohydrate intake, the intake of dietary protein and dietary fibre should be increased and the intake of individual macronutrients should be selected with the consideration of their individual metabolic consequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

dietary weight management should be focused on the reduction of energy intake, the reduction of fat (particularly saturated fat) and simple carbohydrate intake, the increase of dietary protein and the consumption of low glycaemic index, high fibre and high n-3 fatty acid containing foods as well as the intake of sufficient amounts of dietary calcium, phosphate and retinol.
dietary factors play a significant role in the prevention and management of obesity.
the dietary weight management should be targeted on the intake of low energy density foods (i.e. low in fat and high in fibre), low glycaemic index carbohydrate and protein rich diet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dietary weight management should be based on the reduction of energy intake and the intake of fat and carbohydrate with high energy density.

the nutritional approach to the weight management should be based on a balanced, energy-controlled diet rich in fibre, low-glycaemic index carbohydrates, n-3 and polyunsaturated fatty acids and proteins.
dietary factors play a key role in the prevention and treatment of obesity.
